reason: While the text does describe the Hebrew people suffering greatly under Egyptian oppression ('I have heard the cry of the children of Israel and I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them'), the passage shows God acknowledging this suffering with compassion and calling a leader (Moses) to deliver them from it. There is no instance of leaders blaming the people for their suffering. Instead, God takes the initiative to address their distress, demonstrating that He recognizes the injustice of their situation rather than attributing it to their fault.
